about: S3.4 citation checker, spec test T07 — the TUNING set. Fictional documents only. Expectations are what a careful lawyer checking the citations by hand would conclude, written before the check was run on them. G5–G7 were the first held-out set; they became tuning data once they informed a change.

sources.title: Supply Agreement
sources.text:
SUPPLY AGREEMENT (fictional)

1. Definitions

5. Delivery

citing.title: Memo on supply terms
citing.text:
MEMORANDUM (fictional)

1. Delivery
1.1 Clause 5.1 of the Supply Agreement requires delivery "within fourteen (14) days of each Order." Risk passes on delivery under clause 5.2 of the Supply Agreement.
1.2 Clause 5.3 of the Supply Agreement deals with late delivery.

2. Liability
2.1 Clause 9.1 of the Supply Agreement provides that "[t]he Supplier's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Price paid in the preceding six months."
2.2 The products are listed in Schedule 1 of the Supply Agreement and the prices in Schedule 2 of the Supply Agreement.

citing.title: Brief extract
citing.text:
BRIEF EXTRACT (fictional)

1. The claim arises under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 and 28 U.S.C. § 1331.
2. The standard is set out in Palmer v. Oakridge Freight, 544 F.3d 210 (7th Cir. 2008), and Lindqvist v. Harrow Corp., 87 F. Supp. 3d 455 (S.D.N.Y. 2015).
3. A contrary view appears in Morrow v. Pell Industries, 310 F.4th 88 (12th Cir. 2022) and Quist v. Delane, 45 F.6th 12 (9th Cir. 2019).
4. In England, see [2017] UKSC 59, [2008] UKHL 48 and [2016] UKHL 7; and Hadley v Baxendale (1854) 9 Exch 341.
5. In the EU, see Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Directive 2011/83/EU and Case C-311/18.
6. Employers must also follow 29 C.F.R. § 1910.1200.

expect.text: Palmer v. Oakridge Freight, 544 F.3d 210 (7th Cir. 2008)

citing.title: Letter to the client
citing.text:
LETTER (fictional)

1. The Lease says the Tenant "shall pay the Rent quarterly in advance on the Quarter Days."
2. Clause 4.1 of the Lease provides that "The Landlord shall keep the structure and exterior of the Building in good repair."
3. The Lease also states that "The Rent shall be reviewed every five years to open market value."
4. We note the suggestion that "the Tenant may assign this lease freely and without any consent", which we do not accept.

sources.title: Share Purchase Agreement
sources.text:
SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT (fictional)

6. Warranties
6.1 The Seller warrants to the Buyer that each Warranty is true and accurate at the date of this Agreement.
6.2 The Warranties are qualified by matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
6.3 No claim may be brought for breach of Warranty unless notified within eighteen (18) months after Completion.

7. Limitations
7.1 The Seller's aggregate liability for all Claims shall not exceed the Purchase Price.
7.2 The Seller is not liable for a Claim of less than GBP 25,000 (fictional).

Schedule 4 Warranties
1. The Company has filed all tax returns when due.

citing.title: Disclosure memo
citing.text:
DISCLOSURE MEMORANDUM (fictional)

1. Background
1.1 This memo concerns the Share Purchase Agreement (the "SPA").

2. Time limits
2.1 Under section 6.3 of the Share Purchase Agreement, claims must be notified "within eighteen (18) months after Completion".
2.2 By clause 7.2 of the SPA, the Seller is not liable for small claims.

3. Warranties
3.1 Clause 6.2 of the Share Purchase Agreement qualifies the Warranties by "matters disclosed in the Disclosure Letter".
3.2 The tax warranty is paragraph 1 of Schedule 4 of the Share Purchase Agreement; the property warranties are in Schedule 5 of the Share Purchase Agreement.
3.3 Clause 7.1 of the Share Purchase Agreement caps liability at "the Purchase Price" and clause 7.4 of the Share Purchase Agreement excludes consequential loss.
